question.latex: A planet $$P_1$$ is moving around the star of mass $2M$ in the orbit of radius $R$. Another planet $$P_2$$ is moving around another star of mass $4M$ in a orbit of radius $2R$. Ratio of time periods of revolution of $P_2$ and $P_1$ is _______.
question.unicode: A planet P_1 is moving around the star of mass 2M in the orbit of radius R. Another planet P_2 is moving around another star of mass 4M in a orbit of radius 2R. Ratio of time periods of revolution of P_2 and P_1 is _______.
question.plainText: A planet P_1 is moving around the star of mass 2M in the orbit of radius R. Another planet P_2 is moving around another star of mass 4M in a orbit of radius 2R. Ratio of time periods of revolution of P_2 and P_1 is _______.

explanation.latex:
According to Kepler's Third Law and universal gravitation, the time period of a planet revolves around a star of mass $M_{star}$ in an orbit of radius $r$ is given by:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{r^3}{GM_{star}}}$
For planet $P_1$:
$T_1 = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{R^3}{G(2M)}}$
For planet $P_2$:
$T_2 = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{(2R)^3}{G(4M)}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{8R^3}{4GM}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{2R^3}{GM}}$
The ratio of time periods is:
$\frac{T_2}{T_1} = \frac{\sqrt{2R^3 / GM}}{\sqrt{R^3 / 2GM}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{1/2}} = \sqrt{4} = 2$.
explanation.unicode:

T = 2π √((r³/GM_{star))}

T_1 = 2π √((R³/G(2M)))
For planet P_2:
T_2 = 2π √(((2R)³/G(4M))) = 2π √((8R³/4GM)) = 2π √((2R³/GM))
The ratio of time periods is:
(T_2/T_1) = frac{√(2R³ / GM)}{√(R³ / 2GM)} = √((2/1/2)) = √(4) = 2.

question.latex: If a body of mass $1\text{ kg}$ falls on the earth from infinity, it attains velocity $$v$$ and kinetic energy $$k$$ on reaching the surface of earth. The values of $v$ and $k$ respectively are _______. $Take radius of earth to be $6400\text{ km}$ and $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$$
question.unicode: If a body of mass 1text{ kg} falls on the earth from infinity, it attains velocity v and kinetic energy k on reaching the surface of earth. The values of v and k respectively are _______. Take radius of earth to be 6400text{ km} and g = 9.8text{ m/s}²
question.plainText: If a body of mass 1text{ kg} falls on the earth from infinity, it attains velocity v and kinetic energy k on reaching the surface of earth. The values of v and k respectively are _______. Take radius of earth to be 6400text{ km} and g = 9.8text{ m/s}^2

explanation.latex:
By conservation of energy, the kinetic energy attained by falling from infinity is equal to the magnitude of potential energy at the surface of the Earth: $K = \frac{GMm}{R} = mgR$.
Given $m = 1\text{ kg}, g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2, R = 6400 \times 10^3\text{ m}$.
$K = 1 \times 9.8 \times 6400 \times 10^3 = 62.72 \times 10^6\text{ J} = 6.272 \times 10^7\text{ J}$.
The velocity attained is the escape velocity $v = \sqrt{2gR} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6} = \sqrt{125.44 \times 10^6} = 11.2 \times 10^3\text{ m/s} = 11.2\text{ km/s}$.
